title: Decode Ways
statement: A message of digits encodes A as 1 through Z as 26. Return how many ways `s` can be decoded. A leading zero makes a code invalid.
hints: A single digit from 1 to 9 is a letter. 0 is not.
A two-digit window from 10 to 26 is also a letter.
dp[i] adds dp[i - 1] when the last digit is valid and dp[i - 2] when the last two digits are valid.

approaches.name: Recursion on the index
approaches.explanation: Two choices when both windows are legal.

editorial: This is climbing stairs with validity filters. A zero can only survive as the second digit of 10 or 20. If a position can be reached by neither a one-digit nor a two-digit code, the whole string has zero decodings.
